{{< include _model.qmd >}}

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
# GENERATED FROM THIS CHAPTER'S OWN _fork.yml (rule 35 keeps this block here).
# One source, three readers: rule 31 checks this file, the book index draws the
# lineage from it, and this prints what the fork actually changed.
#
# In a CALLOUT, like the Specified and Assumed it sits above. As a bare
# paragraph and a bare list it was the one un-styled region on the page, and it
# read as a mistake rather than as a section. One change renders as a sentence;
# a single-item bullet list is heavier than the sentence it replaced.
import pathlib
import re
_fk = pathlib.Path("chapters/06-fully-optimized-5mm/_fork.yml")
if _fk.exists():
    _t = _fk.read_text()
    _p = re.search(r"^parent:\s*(.+?)\s*$", _t, re.M)
    _items, _in = [], False
    for _l in _t.splitlines():
        if _l.startswith("#") or not _l.strip():
            continue
        if re.match(r"^\w+:", _l):
            _in = _l.startswith("changes:")
            continue
        if _in and _l.lstrip().startswith("-"):
            _items.append(_l.lstrip()[1:].strip())
        elif _in and _items and _l.startswith(" "):
            _items[-1] += " " + _l.strip()
    if _p:
        _par = pathlib.Path("chapters") / _p.group(1) / "index.qmd"
        _pt = re.search(r'^title:\s*"(.+)"\s*$', _par.read_text(), re.M) \
            if _par.exists() else None
        _name = _pt.group(1) if _pt else _p.group(1)
        print('::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}')
        print(f"## Forked from [{_name}](../{_p.group(1)}/)\n")
        if len(_items) == 1:
            print(f"{_items[0]}\n")
        else:
            for _i in _items:
                print(f"* {_i}")
            print()
        print(":::\n")
```

A 300 mm span glider cut from 5 mm foam where almost all geometry (sweep, dihedral, tail area, boom length, tail incidence) is optimized for minimum sink rate in trimmed glide. Adds stability constraints: 10% minimum static margin, plus lateral and directional stability.

::: {.callout-tip}
## New user specifications

1. **Foam thickness**: 5 mm.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## New assumptions

1. **Foam density**: 174.4 g/m² for 5 mm foam.
2. **Airfoil thickness**: 5% to match foam.
:::
